title: Administering, dispensing, prescribing and delivering narcotic drugs for maintenance or detoxification treatment
subtopic: Narcotic drugs for maintenance and detoxification treatment
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1306.07(a) a practitioner may administer or dispense directly (but not prescribe) a narcotic drug in Schedule II to a narcotic dependent person for the purpose of maintenance or detoxification treatment if the practitioner is separately registered with DEA as a narcotic treatment program and is in compliance with DEA regulations regarding treatment qualifications, security, records, and unsupervised use of the drugs pursuant to the Act. Under 1306.07(b) nothing in the section prohibits a practitioner who is not specifically registered to conduct a narcotic treatment program from dispensing (but not prescribing) narcotic drugs, in accordance with applicable Federal, State, and local laws relating to controlled substances, to one person or for one person's use at one time for the purpose of initiating maintenance treatment or detoxification treatment (or both); not more than a three-day supply may be dispensed to the person or for the person's use at one time while arrangements are being made for referral for treatment, and such emergency treatment may not be renewed or extended. Under 1306.07(c) the section is not intended to impose any limitations on a physician or authorized hospital staff to administer or dispense narcotic drugs in a hospital to maintain or detoxify a person as an incidental adjunct to medical or surgical treatment of conditions other than addiction, or to administer or dispense narcotic drugs to persons with intractable pain in which no relief or cure is possible or none has been found after reasonable efforts. Under 1306.07(d) a practitioner may administer or dispense (including prescribe) any Schedule III, IV, or V narcotic drug for use in maintenance or detoxification treatment to a narcotic dependent person. Under 1306.07(f), notwithstanding the definition of dispense in 21 U.S.C. 802(10), a pharmacy may deliver a controlled substance to a practitioner, pursuant to a prescription that meets the requirements of 21 CFR 1306.04, for the purpose of administering the controlled substance by the practitioner if: it is delivered to the prescribing practitioner or the administering practitioner at the location listed on the practitioner's DEA certificate of registration; it is a narcotic drug in Schedule III, IV, or V to be administered for the purpose of maintenance or detoxification treatment by injection or implantation; the pharmacy, the prescribing practitioner and the administering practitioner are authorized to conduct those activities under the law of the State in which they take place; the prescription is not issued to supply any practitioner with a stock of controlled substances for the purpose of general dispensing to patients; it is to be administered only to the patient named on the prescription not later than 45 days after the date of receipt of the controlled substance by the practitioner; and the prescribing and administering practitioners, as applicable, maintain complete and accurate records of all controlled substances delivered, received, administered, or otherwise disposed of under paragraph (f), including the persons to whom the controlled substances were delivered.
exam_relevance: Tests which actor may administer, dispense or prescribe which narcotic drugs for maintenance or detoxification treatment, the limits on the three-day dispensing provision, and the conditions on a pharmacy's delivery of a Schedule III, IV or V narcotic drug to a practitioner for administration by injection or implantation.

numeric_facts.fact: maximum supply dispensed at one time by a practitioner not registered to conduct a narcotic treatment program
numeric_facts.conditions: to initiate maintenance or detoxification treatment while arrangements are being made for referral for treatment; the emergency treatment may not be renewed or extended

numeric_facts.fact: period within which a Schedule III, IV or V narcotic drug delivered under paragraph (f) is to be administered
numeric_facts.conditions: after the date of receipt of the controlled substance by the practitioner, only to the patient named on the prescription

exceptions: Paragraph (c): the section is not intended to impose any limitations on a physician or authorized hospital staff to administer or dispense narcotic drugs in a hospital to maintain or detoxify a person as an incidental adjunct to medical or surgical treatment of conditions other than addiction, or to administer or dispense narcotic drugs to persons with intractable pain in which no relief or cure is possible or none has been found after reasonable efforts.
common_confusions: Paragraphs (a) and (b) both exclude prescribing; paragraph (d), which includes prescribing, is confined to Schedule III, IV and V narcotic drugs.
The three-day dispensing under paragraph (b) may not be renewed or extended.
Under paragraph (f) the 45 days run from the practitioner's receipt of the controlled substance.
verification_notes: Read in the current eCFR text of 21 CFR 1306.07 on 2026-09-14. Paragraphs (g) and (h), on emergency medical services, are not carried by this rule.
